A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the TD learning objective is contractive with respect to the stationary distribution of policies.
we propose to use likelihood-free importance sampling to weight experiences for TD learning, and show empirically that it can accelerate the learning of value functions and policies.
we propose to use the stationary likelihood ratio as the prioritization weight for experience replay, and empirically show that it improves sample efficiency over 3 state-of-the-art algorithms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
likelihood-free importance weighting can be applied to accelerate experience replay for deep reinforcement learning, and that it is competitive with the best baseline in most tasks.
likelihood-free importance weighting can be a simple, yet powerful tool for improving the sample complexity of reinforcement learning algorithms.
prioritizing past experiences based on their importance under a stationary policy can be used to accelerate TD learning.
